chunks: Eat what is lawful and good of the provisions God has bestowed on you, and fear God in whom you believe.

key_terms.اتَّقُوا: Fear or be conscious of God
key_terms.حَلَالًا: Lawful or permissible according to Sharia

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for food to be halal and tayyib in Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Ma'idah is often cited to establish the principle that lawful sustenance must be both ritually pure and ethically sourced, reflecting the holistic nature of worship. It underscores the connection between physical consumption and spiritual consciousness (taqwa), reminding believers that their faith is validated through mindful adherence to divine provisions.
